research.topic: The International Rhino Foundation's State of the Rhino 2024 puts the world's wild rhinos at about 27,000: roughly 17,500 white, 6,400 black, 4,000 greater one-horned, fewer than 50 Sumatran and about 76 Javan. South Africa holds around 16,000 (about 13,000 white and 2,000–2,500 black; DFFE 2024), roughly 6 in 10 of all rhinos. India holds about 4,000, almost all greater one-horned, around 2,600 of them in Kaziranga (Assam Forest Department census 2022). Kenya holds about 2,000 (KWS 2023). Kruger National Park has the largest single rhino population in the world, despite poaching losses (SANParks). The 2 African species are the white and the black rhino; the 3 Asian species are the greater one-horned, Sumatran and Javan.

myths.reality: Kenya holds about 2,000 rhinos; South Africa holds around 16,000, roughly 6 in 10 of the world's total.
